headline: Highest risk is medium: Airflow can egress broadly and Authelia can broker auth, creating default-path leakage and workflow-conflict risks, but no direct shared-channel evidence is provided.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between Airflow and Authelia, and neither profile shows clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridging. Airflow has broad egress, but Authelia only exposes OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth, so an injection pathway is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low because the needed bridge is absent in both profiles.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between Airflow and Authelia, reassess injection risk.
IF Authelia is configured to parse Airflow-generated text as policy or commands, reassess.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate channels with no shared inbox or workspace.
Disable any copy-paste or file-drop workflow between them.
Add provenance labels to any exchanged text.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type validation on any future bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, and Authelia participates in OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth, so a leakage path exists if shared data is routed through auth flows. However, neither profile shows sensitive data classes touched, and no shared workspace or authenticated principal is documented. This is a plausible but small-blast-radius risk in the current profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is given secrets, PHI, or customer data, leakage severity increases.
IF both agents are placed under the same OAuth principal or shared workspace, reassess upward.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets through either agent's prompts or logs.
Use separate service accounts for Airflow and Authelia.
Review outbound destinations for Airflow before enabling jobs.
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow can make API calls and Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping mutable resource scopes. The pair therefore has limited direct write-conflict surface. Because the orchestrator and locking behavior are undocumented, uncertainty remains and is resolved conservatively at low.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external resource, reassess conflict risk.
IF an orchestrator without locking is introduced, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep mutable resources partitioned by service.
Assign distinct OAuth clients and scopes.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared configs.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow commonly produces workflow outputs, and Authelia can act as an auth gateway via ForwardAuth/OIDC, so Airflow-generated artifacts could be consumed downstream without verification. The profiles do not prove this exact pipeline, but the interaction is plausible and default-safe verification is not documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Authelia consumes Airflow output as policy or routing input without validation, reassess upward.
IF Airflow outputs are used to trigger auth decisions or access grants, reassess upward.
mitigations: Insert a human or automated verification step before acting on Airflow output.
Require schema validation on any Airflow-to-Authelia handoff.
Log and review all downstream auth decisions.
requires-engineering: add signed artifacts between systems.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Airflow and Authelia are both open/source-available infrastructure components with no profile evidence of PHI, EU-only data, or conflicting compliance regimes. With no compliance-specific pathway shown, the pairwise compliance risk is provably unsubstantiated here.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes, reassess compliance mapping.
IF residency or retention policies diverge, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents until policies are defined.
Review retention settings if logs are enabled.
